newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: VLCC to resume crude discharge at SRC soon - BP.
newsitem.headline: VLCC to resume crude discharge at SRC soon - BP.

text.p: British Petroleum (BP) said on Monday its tanker will resume discharging crude soon at Singapore Refining Co's (SRC) refinery after operations were stopped earlier in the day following an oil spill.
"Ship's operations already restarted, ballasting in progess, cargo discharge to restart as soon as possible," BP spokesman Matthew Yap said in a written reply to a Reuters query.
The total crude cargo was 240,000 tonnes, he said.

BP said that "an estimated three to four cubic metres of oil was seen in the vicinity of the vessel and this has been dispersed" and operations at the 285,000-barrel-per-day refinery was not affected.
The Singapore Refining Co (SRC) facility is located at Pulau Merlimau, an island off southwestern Singapore.

Industry sources said the very large crude carrier (VLCC), British Reliance, was discharging the Arab Medium crude cargo belonging to Caltex when some ballast or engine oil was found near the single buoy mooring (SBM).
Discharge operations were stopped but the tanker was not disconnected from the SBM.
Divers were sent to check if the oil leaked from the SBM but no leaks were found, sources said.
A Singapore Maritime and Port Authority (MPA) official told Reuters that the MPA was investigating the spill.
She said that the source of the spill is not known.
SRC is jointly-owned by BP, Singapore Petroleum Co and Caltex, itself a joint-venture between Chevron Corp and Texaco Inc.
